summary: Dedicated customer reports bursty p99 latency spikes/timeouts; correlated with KV cache fragmentation under mixed sequence lengths
description:
Issue summary
- Northstar Analytics (Dedicated) reports bursty p99 latency spikes and intermittent request timeouts during traffic bursts.
- Spikes appear to be isolated to specific burst windows (10–20 minutes) and are worst on long-context + mixed-length traffic.

Customer-reported impact
- Customer impact window(s): 2025-02-11 ~15:20–16:05 UTC; additional smaller spikes 2025-02-12 ~09:10–09:25 UTC.
- Symptoms: chat completions p99 latency up from typical ~450–650ms/token decode p99 to 2–6s (end-to-end requests exceeding 30s timeout for some clients); increased 5xx/timeouts from client perspective.
- Business impact: degraded end-user experience during peak usage; customer requesting RCA + mitigation plan and a date for a durable fix.

Environment
- Dedicated pool: ded-northstar-gpu-a100-01 (us-east-1)
- Runtime: serving-runtime 2.31.0 (release train 2025.02.10)
- Traffic characteristics (from customer & traces): bursty arrival rate; mixed context lengths (2k–32k); concurrency spikes from batch jobs + interactive traffic.

Initial triage / observations (Support + SRE)
- Correlation between tail-latency spikes and GPU memory allocator churn in the serving runtime.
- Multiple occurrences of KV cache allocation retries and increased eviction activity during bursts.
- Fragmentation signal (internal allocator stats) rises sharply before p99/p999 degrade; symptoms consistent with known issue: KV cache fragmentation under bursts/mixed seq-len.

What we believe is happening
- Under bursty decode + mixed-length sequences, KV cache block utilization becomes uneven (holes after sequences complete/evict). The allocator spends more time searching/compacting/rehoming (currently limited) and falls back to expensive paths (reallocations / admission control), creating tail spikes.
- This condition also increases OOM risk; the scheduler becomes more conservative (backpressure) which can amplify queueing latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (2025-02-11)
- Increased headroom by raising min replicas in the Dedicated pool (autoscaling floor) for the impacted model routes.
- Temporarily tightened admission control thresholds to reduce allocator churn (tradeoff: some throughput reduction during peaks).
- Shifted a portion of traffic to secondary capacity within the Dedicated reservation (where available) during the burst window.

Customer communications
- Promised: interim mitigation steps + ongoing monitoring + link to durable fix project (KV cache compaction improvements) and expected rollout sequence.

Next steps / internal follow-ups
1) Confirm fragmentation ratio + allocation failure rate at the exact spike times (SRE + runtime).
2) Validate workload reproduction in perf suite (bursty-mix scenario) and quantify baseline vs mitigated behavior.
3) Track customer pool as an early candidate for compaction canary once runtime flag is ready, subject to risk review and customer approval.

References
- Incident coordination: #incidents thread (INC-2025-02-11-USE1-DED-LLM-TAIL)
- Known issue: KV cache fragmentation under bursts (Confluence)
- Planned durable fix: KV cache compaction improvements (ENG-2841; design doc + ADRs)

Requested from customer
- A sample of client-side traces for the timeout requests (request ids/timestamps) and confirmation of client timeout settings.
- Confirmation whether workload mix changed (context length / concurrency) starting Feb 11.

resolution: Mitigated via Dedicated pool capacity headroom + tighter long-context admission control to reduce KV cache allocator churn. Root cause consistent with KV cache fragmentation under bursty mixed-length traffic. Durable fix (compaction-capable allocator + scheduler-aware eviction/trigger budgeting) tracked under ENG-2841 and related runtime PR series; will roll out behind a runtime flag with canary prior to broad enablement.
customer_facing_summary: We observed that the latency spikes coincided with GPU memory (KV cache) allocation/eviction churn during bursty, mixed context-length traffic. We applied mitigations to add headroom and reduce allocator thrash, which stabilized timeouts. We are implementing a more durable KV cache compaction strategy to reduce fragmentation and improve tail latency stability; this will be rolled out behind a safety flag and validated via canary before broad enablement.
